summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease, chronic hepatitis C, and high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was admitted for nausea and left knee pain following her third cycle of cisplatin and doxorubicin chemotherapy. She had poor response to oral antiemetics, leading to dehydration and significant fatigue. Her white blood cell count rose sharply, consistent with an exaggerated response to filgrastim, but there was no evidence of infection. She developed worsening anemia with hemoglobin dropping to 6.9 g/dL, prompting a transfusion of one unit of antigen-matched packed red blood cells. Nausea was managed with intravenous antiemetics and fluids, and pain was controlled with hydromorphone, transitioning from IV to oral. By discharge, she was tolerating oral intake, afebrile, and hemodynamically stable, with improving lab values. She was discharged home with instructions to hold filgrastim until oncology follow-up and to continue home medications for pain, nausea, and chronic conditions.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Malignant neoplasm of long bones of lower limb
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
